concepts.title: Quadratic Function
concepts.description: A quadratic function is a function whose highest power of the variable is two, usually written as ax² + bx + c, with a nonzero.

concepts.title: First and second differences
concepts.description: First differences compare consecutive terms, while second differences compare consecutive first differences and reveal quadratic patterns in sequences.

concepts.title: Completing the square
concepts.description: Completing the square rewrites a quadratic expression in vertex form, making its turning point and minimum or maximum value easier to identify.

concepts.title: Complex numbers
concepts.description: Complex numbers combine real and imaginary parts and use i, where i² = -1, to represent solutions that are not real numbers.

concepts.title: Parabola
concepts.description: A parabola is the U-shaped graph of a quadratic function, defined by its vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts, and direction of opening.

concepts.title: Focus
concepts.description: The focus is the fixed point used to define a parabola, with every point on the curve having a specific relationship to the focus and directrix.

concepts.title: Argand diagram
concepts.description: An Argand diagram represents a complex number as a point or vector, using the horizontal axis for the real part and the vertical axis for the imaginary part.

concepts.title: Related roots
concepts.description: Related roots are connected solutions of a polynomial equation, often occurring in conjugate pairs or through relationships between the coefficients and roots.

concepts.title: Exponential functions
concepts.description: An exponential function has the variable in its exponent and models repeated multiplication, growth, or decay using a positive constant base.

concepts.title: Logarithmic function
concepts.description: A logarithmic function is the inverse of an exponential function and gives the exponent needed to produce a particular value.

concepts.title: Growth
concepts.description: Exponential growth describes a quantity that increases by the same percentage or factor over equal time intervals.

concepts.title: Decay
concepts.description: Exponential decay describes a quantity that decreases by the same percentage or factor over equal time intervals.

concepts.title: Trigonometric functions
concepts.description: Trigonometric functions relate angles to ratios or coordinates and include sine, cosine, and tangent, which describe periodic relationships.

concepts.title: Coordinates
concepts.description: Coordinates locate points on a plane and provide the numerical values needed to describe positions, graphs, and transformations.

concepts.title: Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent functions
concepts.description: These graphs show the periodic patterns, intercepts, maximum and minimum values, and asymptotes of the sine, cosine, and tangent functions.

concepts.title: Inverses of the sine, cosine and tangent functions
concepts.description: Inverse trigonometric functions find an angle from a trigonometric ratio, with their domains and ranges restricted to give defined principal values.

concepts.title: Shape, domain, range, amplitude, intercepts, max/min, period, asymptotes
concepts.description: These features describe the complete behaviour of a trigonometric graph, including its allowed inputs, outputs, scale, crossings, repetition, and undefined values.

concepts.title: Domain of trigonometric functions
concepts.description: The domain of a trigonometric function is the set of input values for which the function is defined, excluding values that create undefined ratios or asymptotes.

concepts.title: Shift and stretch a trigonometric function
concepts.description: Shifts and stretches transform a trigonometric graph by changing its position, amplitude, period, or midline without changing its basic function family.

concepts.title: Trigonometric identities
concepts.description: Trigonometric identities are equations that remain true for every value in their common domain and help simplify expressions and solve equations.

concepts.title: Pythagorean Identities
concepts.description: Pythagorean identities connect the squares of sine, cosine, and tangent and provide fundamental relationships for simplifying trigonometric expressions.

concepts.title: Cofunction Identities
concepts.description: Cofunction identities relate a trigonometric function of an angle to its complementary function, such as sine and cosine.

concepts.title: Trig identities of sum and difference of two angels
concepts.description: Sum and difference identities expand the sine, cosine, or tangent of two combined angles into expressions involving the individual angles.

concepts.title: Trig identities of double angles and half angels
concepts.description: Double-angle and half-angle identities rewrite trigonometric expressions involving twice an angle or half an angle into useful equivalent forms.

concepts.title: System
concepts.description: A system is a collection of related equations or inequalities considered together to find values that satisfy all of them.

concepts.title: System of equations
concepts.description: A system of equations contains multiple equations whose common solution satisfies every equation at the same time.

concepts.title: Unknowns
concepts.description: Unknowns are variables whose values must be determined from the equations, conditions, or constraints in a mathematical model.

concepts.title: Graphing methods
concepts.description: Graphing methods solve or analyse equations by plotting relationships and identifying intersection points, regions, and boundary lines.

concepts.title: Algebraic methods
concepts.description: Algebraic methods solve systems by manipulating equations through substitution, elimination, or equivalent transformations.

concepts.title: Matrix
concepts.description: A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers used to organize coefficients, represent transformations, and solve systems of equations.

concepts.title: Operations
concepts.description: Matrix operations include addition, scalar multiplication, and multiplication, each following rules based on dimensions and corresponding entries.

concepts.title: Linear Programming
concepts.description: Linear programming finds the maximum or minimum value of an objective function while satisfying a set of linear constraints.

concepts.title: Objective functions
concepts.description: An objective function expresses the quantity to be maximized or minimized in a linear programming problem.

concepts.title: Feasible regions
concepts.description: The feasible region is the set of points that satisfies all linear programming constraints and contains the possible solutions.

concepts.title: Constraints
concepts.description: Constraints are equations or inequalities that limit the possible values of variables in a mathematical model.

concepts.title: Optimal solution
concepts.description: An optimal solution is the feasible point that gives the greatest or least value of the objective function, depending on the problem goal.

concepts.title: Determinants
concepts.description: A determinant is a scalar calculated from a square matrix that provides information about invertibility, scaling, and related geometric properties.

concepts.title: Value of a determinant
concepts.description: The value of a determinant is found from the entries of a square matrix and can be used to test whether the matrix has an inverse.

concepts.title: Area, parallelogram and triangle
concepts.description: Determinants can calculate the area of a parallelogram or triangle formed by vectors or coordinate points.

concepts.title: Matrices
concepts.description: Matrices organize numbers into rows and columns and provide a structured way to represent transformations and systems of equations.

concepts.title: System of equations
concepts.description: A system of equations can be represented in matrix form and solved using determinants, elimination, or matrix methods.

concepts.title: Cramer Rule
concepts.description: Cramer's rule solves a system of linear equations by replacing columns of the coefficient matrix and comparing the resulting determinants.
